For more information on M-series availability by regions and for upcoming region launches, please visit the Azure regions page. Learn more about running SAP workloads on Azure

Title: Threat intelligence-based filtering for Azure Firewall is now available in preview
Summary: Threat intelligence-based filtering for Azure Firewall is now available in preview. The addition of the Threat Intelligence feed to the filtering capabilities expands both the options to alert and deny traffic from/to known malicious IP addresses and domains based on near real-time data sourced from the Microsoft Threat Intelligence feed powered by the Intelligent Security Graph and used by multiple services across Azure and Microsoft. Support for Service Tags, which has also been a highly reque...

Title: General Availability: Azure Lab Services
Summary: Azure Lab Services is now generally available. Azure Lab services enables you to easily set up and provide on-demand access to labs of preconfigured virtual machines. Provide a simple and interactive hands-on learning experience on the virtual machines to teach a class, train professionals, and run hackathons, among other activities. General availability pricing will go into effect May 1, 2019. To learn more, visit Azure Lab Services .

Title: Continuous integration and deployment to Azure API Management
Summary: The ability to separate Azure API Management service instances for various environments—for example, production, staging, or QA—is now available in preview. These environments are usually shared by multiple development teams, each responsible for a subset of APIs. In addition, we’ve published a conceptual framework for achieving continuous integration and deployment, and , we’ve provided utility tools and examples to help achieve continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD).The tools are open s...

Title: Microsoft Azure Logic Apps Connector for 3270 Screens available now in Public Preview
Summary: Azure Logic Apps with the new 3270 connector allows enterprise developers to build modern applications that automate end user task flows based on legacy IBM mainframe 3270 programs, and to deliver robotic process automation (RPA) and other integration capabilities. Using Logic Apps with the new 3270 connector, enterprise developers can more easily build new composite applications and APIs that incorporate existing line-of-business 3270-based mainframe programs with modern cloud services, to sign...

Title: New capabilities in Azure Monitor alerts
Summary: There are two new capabilities with Azure Monitor metric alerts: Multi-resource metric alerts allow you to create a single metric alert rule that will be applicable for multiple virtual machines. For example, create a single alert for all virtual machines in a resource group. Learn more about multi-resource metric alerts in this blog post . Dynamic thresholds uses machine learning capabilities to decide the right thresholds for your alerts automatically, so you don’t need to guess the thresholds...

Title: Azure Monitor Log Analytics is now available in Azure China
Summary: Azure Monitor Log Analytics is now available in Azure China. Azure Monitor is a fully managed monitoring service that collects and analyzes telemetry from your Azure and on-premises resources and applications allowing you to maximize their performance. Please see the products by region page to see the capabilities coming to Azure China. Visit the Azure Monitor documentation page .

Title: Extended Security Updates for SQL Server 2008 are available now
Services: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
Summary: On July 9, 2019, support for SQL Server 2008 and 2008 R2 will end. That means the end of regular security updates. Don't let your infrastructure and applications go unprotected. We can help you migrate to current versions for greater security, performance, and innovation, but if you need more time for your modernization project, you may want to purchase the new Extended Security Updates offer for your on-premises deployments of SQL Server 2008/R2. Learn how to prepare for SQL Server 2008 end of...

Title: Retiring Azure Batch AI
Summary: Microsoft made the Azure Machine Learning service generally available on Dec 4, 2018, which allows users to build, train, manage and deploy machine learning models. Because this new service has fully replaced the capabilities of Azure Batch AI Preview, we are retiring Batch AI on March 31, 2019, and customers will need to migrate their models by then. Recommended action Customers should migrate to the Azure Machine Learning service before March 31, 2019, to avoid disruptions to applications and...

Title: General availability: Azure Kubernetes Service in France Central
Summary: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is now generally available in France Central. It's the 18th Azure region to offer the service. In the list of regions , you can see where AKS is available and where it's coming next. AKS offers a fully managed Kubernetes environment on Azure. It enables customers to spend less time managing infrastructure and more time building applications. To learn more, check out the AKS product page and documentation .

Title: .NET Core February 2019 Update availability on App Service
Summary: The .NET Core February 2019 Update has been deployed to all regions for public Azure App Service (Windows), all App Service Environment instances running in public App Service (Windows), all sovereign cloud regions, and all App Service Environment instances running in sovereign cloud regions. For more details on the contents of the .NET Core update, see the NET blog .

Title: Protect on-premises VMs by directly replicating to managed disks in Azure
Summary: Azure Site Recovery now supports disaster recovery of VMware virtual machines and physical machines by directly replicating to managed disks. You don't need to create and manage multiple target storage accounts for replicating your machines anymore. On-premises data will be sent to a cache storage account in the target region and then written into managed disks by Site Recovery. Learn more . Existing replications will continue to replicate to storage accounts.

Title: Global VNet Peering now supports Standard Load Balancer
Summary: Global VNet Peering now supports Standard Load Balancer. Previously, resources in one virtual network could not communicate with the front-end IP address of an internal load balancer over a globally peered connection. The virtual networks needed to be in the same region. With this announcement, this is no longer the case. You can communicate with the internal IP address of a Standard Load Balancer instance across regions from resources deployed in a globally peered virtual network. This support...

Title: General availability: Azure Availability Zones in East US
Summary: Azure Availability Zones , a high-availability solution for mission-critical applications, is now generally available in East US. Availability Zones are physically separate locations within an Azure region. Each Availability Zone consists of one or more datacenters equipped with independent power, cooling, and networking. With the introduction of Availability Zones, we now offer a service-level agreement (SLA) of 99.99% for uptime of virtual machines. Availability Zones are generally available i...

Title: General availability: Global VNet Peering in Azure Government regions
Summary: Global VNet Peering is now generally available in all Azure Government cloud regions. This means you can peer virtual networks across the Azure Government cloud regions. You cannot peer across Azure Government cloud and Azure public cloud regions. Global VNet Peering enables resources in your virtual network to communicate directly, without gateways, extra hops, or transit over the public internet. Communication is completely private and over the Microsoft backbone. This allows a high-bandwidth,...

Title: General availability: Azure Lab Services
Summary: Azure Lab Services is now generally available. With Azure Lab Services, you can set up on-demand access to preconfigured virtual machines. Users go to a single place to access all their VMs across multiple labs. For classroom or professional training, you can provide students with a lab of virtual machines configured with exactly what they need. You can run a hackathon or a hands-on lab at conferences or events and scale up to hundreds of virtual machines for your attendees. You can also create...

Title: Azure DevOps CLI preview and feature updates in Pipelines - Sprint 148 Update
Summary: In the Sprint 148 Update of Azure DevOps, we added a new command-line interface (CLI) extension that allows you to interact with Azure DevOps services by using the command line. In addition, we added new options to the Azure Deployment Center to make it simpler to deploy web apps for Windows, Linux, and Containers to Azure. You can now use Azure Pipelines to deploy these resources from your local Git repo to Azure. We are also releasing a new Azure subscription option in the service connection t...

Title: Power BI Workspace Collections is being retired
Summary: Power BI Workspace Collections is being retired. Migrate to Power BI Embedded by June 30, 2018, for continued support of embedded analytics in your app. By migrating, you’ll avoid service disruptions and gain an improved experience through the simplified API surface. After June 30, 2018, visuals embedded through Power BI Workspace Collections will no longer be viewable in your apps. Application data will be available in the Power BI Workspace Collections service until December 31, 2018. By trans...

Title: Introducing the Azure portal “how to” video series
Summary: A new video weekly series highlights specific aspects of the Azure portal so you can be more efficient and productive while deploying your cloud workloads from the portal. Each video in the series demonstrates how to take advantage of a portal feature or capability, such as: How to work with multiple accounts, directories, and subscriptions in Azure. How to create a virtual machine. How to stay connected to Azure virtual machines by using the Azure mobile app. You can try out the features in the...

Title: Database rename is now supported in Azure SQL Database Managed Instance
Summary: Azure SQL Database Managed Instance enables you to rename databases by using Transact-SQL language: ALTER DATABASE WWI MODIFY NAME = WideWorldImporters; For more details, see the ALTER DATABASE and sp_rename syntax.

Title: Public preview: Azure Log Analytics is available in new regions in Australia
Summary: Azure Log Analytics is part of Azure Monitor. It collects telemetry from a variety of sources and uses the query language from Azure Data Explorer to retrieve and analyze data. Azure Log Analytics is available for preview now in Australia East and in Australia Central.

Title: Azure Container Registry firewall rules and Virtual Network (in preview)
Summary: Firewall rules and Virtual Network support in Azure Container Registry are now available in preview. Limit registry access to your resources in Azure, or specific on-premises resources, including Express Route connected devices. Virtual Network access is provided through the Azure Container Registry premium tier . General availability pricing will be announced at a later date. Learn more Read our blog

Title: Azure App Service - WildFly on Linux is in preview
Summary: WildFly is a fully managed app server running on App Service powered by Azul Zulu JDK, bringing free Java LTS support and maintenance to Azure customers. WildFly on Azure is a standalone instance but can be configured to scale and connect with other Azure services for enterprise-grade performance. Learn more

Title: Remove Application Insights connections via PowerShell
Summary: With OMS portal deprecation for the Azure commercial cloud on January 15, 2019, and for the Azure US Government cloud on March 30, 2019, there is no way to configure and remove existing Application Insights connections from the portal. To stop application data from reaching your workspace, remove existing connections by using a PowerShell script . The recommended alternative method to query multiple Azure Monitor Application Insights resources is using cross-resource searches.

Title: Support for Enterprise Security Package–enabled HDInsight clusters in Azure Data Factory
Summary: You can now use Azure Data Factory to operationalize your Azure HDInsight Spark and Hadoop workloads against HDInsight clusters with Enterprise Security Package (ESP) that are joined to an Active Directory domain. We're introducing a new property, isEspEnabled , in the HDInsight linked service in Azure Data Factory, which you can specify if the cluster is ESP enabled. Because ESP clusters are inside a virtual network, you currently have to set up a self-hosted integration runtime inside the same...

Title: Monitor Azure Data Factory pipelines by using Azure Monitor and Log Analytics
Summary: Azure Data Factory integration with Azure Monitor enables you to route your data factory metrics to Log Analytics. Now, you can monitor the health of your data factory pipelines by using the Azure Data Factory Analytics service pack available in the Azure Marketplace. For more information, read the blog post .

Title: Azure Data Factory visual tools integrated with GitHub
Summary: Azure Data Factory visual tools are now integrated with GitHub (public and enterprise). The GitHub integration helps you collaborate with other developers, do source control, and version your data factory assets (pipelines, datasets, linked services, triggers, and more). For more information, read the blog post .

Title: Self-hosted IR sharing across multiple data factories
Summary: You can share an existing self-hosted integration runtime (IR) with multiple data factories. This functionality helps you reuse an existing self-hosted IR infrastructure in another data factory while building a hybrid data-integration pipeline. For more information, see the blog post .

Title: Parameterize connections to your data stores in Azure Data Factory
Summary: You can now parameterize a linked service in Azure Data Factory. When you create a linked service, select Add Dynamic Content under the property that you want to parameterize. For more information, see the blog post .

Title: Linked Resource Manager template support available for CI/CD in your data factories
Summary: Azure Data Factory now generates linked Azure Resource Manager templates for continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) by breaking the factory payload into several files to help users with Resource Manager template limits. For more information, see the documentation .

Title: Azure Functions now supported as a step in Azure Data Factory pipelines
Summary: Azure Functions is now integrated with Azure Data Factory, so you can run an Azure function as a step in your data factory pipelines. For more information, read the blog post .

Title: Create alerts to proactively monitor your data factory pipelines
Summary: Organizations can now improve operational productivity by creating alerts on data integration events (success/failure) and proactively monitor with Azure Data Factory. For more information, see the blog post .

Title: Enhanced monitoring capabilities and tags/annotations in Azure Data Factory
Summary: Azure Data Factory pipelines now include tagging support and enhanced monitoring capabilities, including dashboards and improved debugging support. For more information, watch the Channel 9 video .

Title: Code-free data transformation at scale using Azure Data Factory
Summary: Azure Data Factory has new code-free visual data transformation capabilities. You can visually design, build, and manage data transformation processes without learning Spark or having a deep understanding of the distributed infrastructure. For more information, watch the Channel 9 video .

Title: Tooling improvements for TypeScript support in Azure Functions
Summary: Visual Studio Code and the Azure Functions Core Tools now allow developers to specify they are using TypeScript and will provide templates to get started on top of a base code already prepared, expediting development. We have also released a set of npm scripts which will abstract some Functions Core Tools commands (func commands), so any TypeScript developer can treat Functions projects as if it was any regular node.js project and work with them on a familiar paradigm. Learn more on the blog

Title: Azure Database for MySQL: Read replica now generally available
Summary: Azure Database for MySQL now supports continuous asynchronous replication of data from one Azure Database for MySQL server (master) to up to five Azure Database for MySQL servers (replicas) in the same region. This allows read-heavy workloads to scale beyond the capacity constraints of one Azure Database for MySQL server and to be balanced across replica servers according to users' preference. Replica servers are read-only except for writes replicated from data changes on the master. Stopping re...

Title: Virtual network service endpoints for Azure Database for MariaDB are now generally available
Summary: Now generally available, virtual network service endpoints for Azure Database for MariaDB are now accessible in all available regions . Virtual network service endpoints allow you to isolate connectivity to your logical server from only a given subnet or set of subnets within your virtual network. Traffic to Azure Database for MariaDB from the virtual network service endpoints stays within the Azure network, preferring this direct route over any specific routes that take internet traffic through...

Title: Instantly provision GraphQL on Azure with Hasura and Azure Database for PostgreSQL
Summary: Azure Database for PostgreSQL users can now take advantage of the Hasura GraphQL Engine , a lightweight, high performance, open source product that instantly provides a real time GraphQL API on a Postgres database. With the GraphQL engine’s admin UI, users can explore their GraphQL APIs and manage their database schemas and data. In addition, the GraphQL engine also allows users to write custom resolvers with schema-stitching and to integrate serverless functions or microservice APIs that get tr...

Title: Data Migration Assistant support for Cassandra to Azure Cosmos DB assessment
Summary: Now in preview, the Data Migration Assistant provides support to help customers with migrating data from Cassandra to Azure Cosmos DB. Running the Data Migration Assistant on Cassandra data detects potential compatibility and feature parity issues that can impact functionality in target Azure Cosmos DB datasets. Learn more

Title: Azure Database for MySQL and PostgreSQL: New compute options are now available
Summary: Microsoft’s open source database services, Azure Database for MySQL and Azure Database for PostgreSQL , now provide users with the ability to scale up compute to 64 vCores in the general purpose pricing tiers and to 32 vCores in the memory optimized tiers. With the general availability release of this increase in compute, Azure Database for MySQL and Azure Database for PostgreSQL can support even larger workloads, helping you to better accommodate future growth. Learn more about Azure Database f...

Title: Azure Functions, Java Support GA
Summary: Java support in Azure Functions 2.0 is now generally available. Write Functions using Java 8 while taking advantage of Maven-powered developer experiences provided by Visual Studio Code, IntelliJ, Eclipse, and the cross-platform Functions Core Tools. Learn more

Title: New features are now generally available in Event Grid
Summary: The following set of features, previously in preview, are now generally available: Retry policies Dead lettering Storage queues as a destination Hybrid connections as a destination Manual validation handshake Learn more in the Azure blog

Title: Azure Maps events in Azure Event Grid
Summary: Azure Maps now integrates with Azure Event Grid so you can respond to geofence events to send event notifications to other services and trigger downstream processes. With this integration, you can react to events when an asset enters a geofence, exits a geofence, or when a geofencing query returns a result. Learn more about reacting to Azure Maps events using Event Grid

Title: Azure Event Grid Availability in Azure US Gov regions
Summary: Azure Event Grid is now generally available in US Gov Texas, Arizona, and Virginia regions for production workloads. Not all event sources are available yet in US Gov regions. Services are being added continually, but currently only custom topics, Azure Resource Manager, storage, Event Hubs, Service Bus, and IoT Hub events are available. Check out the Azure Government documentation to get started

Title: Azure SQL DB as reference data input
Summary: Reference data (also known as a lookup table) is a finite data set that’s static or slowly changing in nature, used to augment your fast-moving data streams. Azure Stream Analytics now natively supports Azure SQL DB as a source of reference data input. Easily author a query to extract the dataset from your Azure SQL DB and configure a refresh interval for scenarios that require slow changing reference datasets. For advanced scenarios, we also support delta queries that simply pull in incremental...

Title: Machine learning-based anomaly detection functions in Azure Stream Analytics (preview)
Summary: Stream Analytics now empowers every developer to easily add anomaly detection capabilities to their Stream Analytics jobs without requiring them to develop and train their own machine learning models. Ready-to-use machine learning models are provided right within the SQL language. This reduces the cost and complexity associated with building and training machine learning models to a simple single function call. Learn more

Title: Azure Policy non-compliance reasoning and change history features
Summary: Azure Policy is the best way to codify company policies into the core of Azure, reducing the time taken with external approval processes and documentation. New functionalities have been added to Azure Policy, including non-compliance reasoning and change history features. This means that you’ll be able to see why a resource evaluated as non-complaint and what changes were implemented directly by a policy. Learn more Try it now

Title: M-series virtual machines (VMs) are now available in the Korea South region
Summary: Azure M-series VMs are now available in the Korea South region. M-series VMs offer configurations with memory from 192 GB to 3.8 TiB (4 TB) RAM and are certified for SAP HANA. For more information on M-series availability by regions and for upcoming region launches, please visit the Azure regions page . Learn more about running SAP workloads on Azure

Title: Azure Blockchain: Updated Hyperledger Fabric template 1.3 now available
Summary: An updated deployment template for Hyperledger Fabric is now generally available . This new Azure Resource Manager template is available in the Azure Marketplace and allows you to configure and deploy a Hyperledger Fabric 1.3 network into your Azure subscriptions with just a few clicks. With this template, you can perform both single virtual machine (VM) (multi container) development and multi VM (scale out) models and connect multi-subscriptions via a private connection. Connect Fabric nodes ru...

Title: Integration Services Environment
Summary: Integration Service Environment is now available in preview and provides a fully isolated and dedicated environment to securely connect cloud and on-premises applications. Learn more

Title: Quickly build data integration pipelines by using templates in Azure Data Factory
Summary: Data Engineers or data developers can now use templates in Azure Data Factory to quickly build data integration pipelines, improve developer productivity, and reduce development time for repeat processes. For more information, see the blog post .

Title: Azure Analysis Services web designer to be discontinued
Summary: The Azure Analysis Services web designer in the Azure portal has been in public preview since it was introduced in July 2017. It was later deprecated in October 2018, meaning that it would be discontinued at some point in the future. We’ve tried to avoid discontinuing it entirely, but due to certain compliance requirements, it will be removed from the portal as early as March 1, 2019. Instead of the web designer, we recommend that you use SQL Server Data Tools and SQL Server Management Studio fo...

Title: Application Insights is now available in Australia East and Japan East
Summary: Azure Application Insights is now available in Australia East and Japan East. Application Insights can monitor applications in any part of the world. Collected data can now be stored locally in these additional regions.

Title: Azure Monitor status blog is now available
Summary: The Azure Monitor Status blog provides timely updates on the health of Azure Monitor products (Application Insights, Log Analytics, Service Map, Azure Alerts). This status blog is managed by our SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) team. It provides detailed information on ongoing outages, planned maintenance events, or advisory notifications. The intention of this blog is to provide transparent communication to all our customers.

Title: Protect Azure VMs by using Storage Spaces Direct with Azure Site Recovery
Summary: Azure Site Recovery now supports disaster recovery of Azure virtual machines by using Storage Spaces Direct . You can use Site Recovery to make your higher-availability application more resilient with the addition of protection against region-level failure. For more information, see the documentation .

Title: Enhancements to NSG flow logs (version 2) for Azure Network Watcher
Summary: Network security group (NSG) flow logs in Azure Network Watcher offer valuable information that help our customers audit their networks in the cloud. Enhancements to the flow logs (version 2) now include byte and packet counts and session state on a per-flow basis. The new metrics provide additional information that can help you better understand capacity utilization and maintain compliance on the network. These enhancements to NSG flow logs are now available in all public cloud regions. Traffic...

Title: OMS Agent for Linux February release now available
Summary: The OMS Agent for Linux February 2019 release is now available. This release contains many stability and reliability improvements. If you have installed the OMS Agent for Linux by using Azure extensions and have automatic extension updates turned on, this update will be automatically applied over the coming weeks. Otherwise, you can use the latest installer available in the agent GitHub repo. For more information, see the agent release notes .

Title: Azure API Management update February 14
Summary: On February 14, we started a regular Azure API Management service update. The update includes the following bug fixes, changes, and new features: You can now use the rate-limit policy at the API and API operation levels in addition to the product scope that was supported before. You can now refer a certificate by its identifier in the authentication-certificate policy. You can now use the set-header policy to modify the Host header that will be forwarded to the back end. You can now use System.S...

Title: Azure Sphere 19.02 Release
Summary: The Azure Sphere 19.02 release is available now. In this release, we focus on broader device capabilities, reducing your time to market through new reference solutions, and continuing to prioritize features based on feedback from organizations that build by using Azure Sphere. For information about all the features that are included in this release, see our blog post .

Summary: We updated the Features Timeline to provide visibility on our key investments for this quarter. Title: Public preview: Power BI Embedded support for application authentication with service principal
Summary: Service principal support for authentication (preview) is now available for applications using Power BI Embedded . Service principal with Power BI Embedded enhances deployment, security, and lifecycle management, allowing applications to authenticate without the requirement for a Power BI Pro user. Service principal is the recommended authentication method to use with Power BI Embedded. Learn more about service principal for authentication with Power BI Embedded . As a best practice, we'll apply the Open Container Initiative (OCI) update to applicable services that we maintain. Summary: Recently, a security vulnerability ( CVE-2019-5736 ) was announced in runC, the low-level container runtime that supports Docker and associated container engines. The vulnerability allows a malicious container to escalate privileges on the host machine when a user runs the exec command to execute an operation in a running instance of that container. Title: Public preview: Azure Service Bus for Node.js
Summary: We're pleased to announce our first preview release of a new package for using Azure Service Bus from your Node.js services. This package provides concise idioms for sending and receiving messages over the AMQP 1.0 protocol as implemented by the github.com/amqp/rhea package. Get started by running `npm install @azure/service-bus`. Title: Azure Automation supports the Azure PowerShell Az module
Summary: Azure Automation now supports the Azure PowerShell Az module . With this support, you can take advantage of the latest Azure modules in your Automation PowerShell runbooks that manage Azure services. Read more about how to import and use the Az module in Automation .

Title: General availability: Azure Kubernetes Service in Australia Southeast
Summary: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is now generally available in Australia Southeast. It's the seventeenth Azure region to offer the service. In the list of regions , you can see where AKS is available and where it's coming next. AKS offers a fully managed Kubernetes environment on Azure. It enables customers to spend less time managing infrastructure and more time building applications. To learn more, check out the AKS product page and documentation .

Title: SQL Database as a source of reference data input for Stream Analytics
Summary: Azure Stream Analytics now natively supports Azure SQL Database as a source of reference data input. Developers can author a query to extract the dataset from Azure SQL Database, and configure a refresh interval for scenarios that require slowly changing reference datasets. Summary: In Azure Stream Analytics, users can optionally specify the number of partitions of a stream when performing repartitioning. This will enable better performance tuning when the partition key can't be changed to upstream constraints, or there's a fixed number of partitions for output, or partitioned processing is needed to scale out to a larger processing load.

Summary: Azure Stream Analytics users can now partition output to Azure Blob storage based on custom date and time formats. This feature greatly improves downstream data-processing workflows by allowing fine-grained control over the blob output, especially for scenarios such as dashboarding and reporting. It also enables stronger alignment with downstream Hive-supported formats and conventions when consumed by services such as Azure HDInsight or Azure Databricks.

Summary: Azure Stream Analytics now supports high-performance and efficient write operations to Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Data Warehouse to help customers achieve four to five times higher throughput than what was previously possible. Summary: Azure Backup already supports backup and restore of virtual machines created through the classic and Azure Resource Manager deployment models, along with Azure Premium Storage VMs. Azure Backup now supports backup and restore of virtual machines encrypted through Azure Disk Encryption. With this release, customers can now back up VMs encrypted through either a BitLocker encryption key or a key encryption key (KEK). Summary: You can use In-Memory OLTP to achieve incredible performance gains (up to 30X) for transaction processing and data ingestion in your Azure SQL Database Premium databases, with no or minimal changes to the application. Summary: Azure API Management now supports SOAP APIs. Customers can take advantage of features—such as security, analytics, and the developer portal—that were previously available only for REST/HTTP-style APIs. A customer can upload a WSDL document that describes their SOAP service. Azure API Management will then generate a SOAP facade, as well as documentation and a test console in the Azure portal. Find out more about this feature ​on the Azure API Management team blog .

Summary: Based on great customer feedback, we’ve redesigned the Azure Functions portal experience. Now you can see more of your code and see your logs and the Run window at the same time. With the latest service update, Azure Cosmos DB can automatically detect GeoJSON fragments that contain Polygon and LineString objects within your documents, and index them for efficient spatial proximity queries. Summary: Azure Cosmos DB now supports IP-based access controls for restricting access to a database account. This IP-based access control model is very similar to the firewall rules of a traditional database system and provides an additional level of security to the Azure Cosmos DB database account. With this model, you can configure a Azure Cosmos DB database account to be accessible only from an approved set of machines and/or cloud services. Title: Akamai Standard supports geo-filtering
Summary: You can now restrict access to your content, by country, for your Akamai profiles directly through the Azure portal. You can find it by selecting your profile and your endpoint in the portal, and finding Geo-Filtering in the left navigation panel. The Verizon Standard and Premium profiles will still use the alternative management portal for now. Check out more details in the Azure documentation .

Title: Azure Cosmos DB portal updates: New metrics blade and improved collection management
Summary: Azure Cosmos DB , a globally replicated and managed NoSQL database service, added a consolidated metrics experience to the Azure portal. Title: Azure App Service Companion preview available for iOS
Summary: On October 10, we released the preview for Azure App Service Companion to the Google Play Store . Today we're expanding the preview to iOS devices. As with the Android version of the app, the focus is to provide the basic functionality that you need when you are on the go, without requiring you to use your laptop. And it's in a native experience for your device. Read more in our blog .

Title: Error handling added to Automation graphical runbooks
Summary: Azure Automation graphical runbooks have been improved with the ability to include error handling. You can now create error links and configure an activity to convert exceptions to errors. This allows a runbook author to catch errors and do custom error handling.

Title: Update: Automation Graphical Authoring SDK
Summary: An update to the public preview of the Microsoft Azure Automation Graphical Authoring SDK has been released. The update includes support for new error-handling features. In particular, there is support for configuring an activity to convert exceptions to errors. Go to Microsoft Azure Automation Graphical Authoring SDK to download the latest version.

Title: Improving Azure App Service Node.js and PHP developer experience with Linux support
Summary: In March 2015, Azure App Service became generally available, making it easier for web developers to do cool things in the cloud. In addition to a great experience for .NET developers, App Service supports PHP, Node.js, Java, and Python stacks, as well as a number of open-source web products. A new public preview introduces native Linux support for Node.js and PHP stacks.

Title: General availability: UltraPerformance Gateway tier for Azure ExpressRoute
Summary: UltraPerformance Gateway connects a virtual network to an Azure ExpressRoute circuit and provides five times the network throughput of HighPerformance Gateway. Customers can now deploy more network-intensive workloads in their virtual networks. For information about pricing, please visit the VPN Gateway pricing page.

Summary: The new Azure Cosmos DB Java and Node.js SDKs are available. Both include support for TOP and ORDER BY queries on partitioned collections . You can use TOP and ORDER BY queries to retrieve the top number of results from multiple partitions in your database and order those results based on the property that you specify. Title: Public preview: SOAP pass-through support for Azure API Management
Summary: Azure API Management now supports SOAP APIs. Summary: Based on customer requests, we updated the HTTP/HTTPS job timeout in Azure Scheduler from 30 seconds to 60 seconds. This change applies to existing and new jobs. To learn more about limits and defaults in Scheduler, visit the Quotas and limits page.

Title: Mobile Apps .NET SDK 3.0.2 released

However, if you are upgrading from version 2.x to get support for Android Nougat, you should use version 3.0.2. Read the full details about this release in our team blog .

With temporal tables, you can see your data as of any point in the past and use a declarative cleanup policy to control retention for the historical data. Summary: We'll retire support for PHP 5.4 in October 2016. If you have an application deployed to Azure App Service that's using PHP 5.4, you have two options: Upgrade to PHP 5.6. Use a custom PHP runtime . We originally announced the retirement of PHP 5.4 in May and have followed up with email communication to customers who are using PHP web applications. For more information on how to migrate your application from PHP 5.4 to another version, review the migration guides on the PHP website.

Summary: Use Process Explorer to manage your website processes, and you'll be able to enumerate different instances of your site, browse processes for each instance, and drill down and view the handles and modules associated with each process. You'll also get get rich monitoring of the CPU, Working Set, and Thread count at the process level to help you identify runaway processes, find open file handles, and even kill a specific process instance.

Title: Server management experiences for SQL Database
Summary: In this update, we have added server management experiences for SQL Database in the new Azure Preview portal. You can now easily reset the server administrator password, and configure firewall rules and default auditing settings for databases in the server.

Title: Preview: Azure Search
Summary: Azure Search is a search-as-a-service solution that allows developers to incorporate search capabilities into their applications without having to worry about the complexities of full-text search or to deploy, maintain or manage any infrastructure. Even as non-experts, developers can construct rich ranking models that connect search results to application or business objectives. For more information, see Azure Search overview . Summary: Azure Backup is now available in Japan East and Japan West with the same service-level agreement coverage available in other regions worldwide. Azure Backup can help you back up and recover data across Windows Server and Microsoft System Center. You can store and recover files, SQL Server database snapshots, and Hyper-V virtual machines in the cloud. For more information about services' regional availability, visit our Azure Regions page .

Title: General Availability: Mobile Services .NET backend
Summary: The Mobile Services .NET backend is generally available. With a .NET backend, you can write your services using the power of ASP.NET Web API and your favorite .NET language. Mobile Services lets you add a cloud-hosted backend to your mobile app and quickly light up functionality such as data storage, authentication, and scalable push notifications. For more information, check out the announcement blog post from Scott Guthrie .

Summary: Azure WebJobs can now be created and managed in the Azure Portal preview. The portal will support On Demand WebJobs and Continuous WebJobs. You can also use the Console to interact with your WebJobs directly, and use the WebJobs SDK to make authoring easier. Learn more about Azure WebJobs .

Summary: Azure Storage includes locally redundant storage, geo-redundant storage, and read-access geo-redundant storage. Now we're adding zone-redundant storage, which has multiple copies replicated across two to three facilities. For more information, visit the Storage webpage. For a comprehensive look at pricing, visit the Storage pricing details webpage.

Summary: Microsoft Antimalware offers customers the ability to install an antimalware agent for both PaaS roles and virtual machines. Based on System Center Endpoint Protection, this new feature brings proven on-premises security technology to the cloud. We offer deep integration for Trend’s Deep Security ™ and SecureCloud ™ products in the Azure platform. DeepSecurity is an Antivirus solution and SecureCloud is an encryption solution. DeepSecurity will be deployed inside of VMs using an extension model...

Title: Deployment slots in Azure Websites expanded to 4+1 slots
Summary: Azure Web Sites has increased the number of deployment slots for Standard websites to 4 (in addition to the Production slot). This gives you more deployment options, since you can keep multiple versions of your site and alternate between them while continuing to develop. Learn more .

Title: Preview: Instance-level public IPs for virtual machines
Summary: Assign public IP addresses to your virtual machines so they become directly addressable, and eliminate the need to map an endpoint for direct access. Once you're done, you'll be able to do things like run FTP servers in Azure and monitor virtual machines directly using their IPs. The virtual machine will also use this public IP as its outgoing IP for all connections that is sourced from this VM. During preview you get two free public IP addresses per subscription. For more information visit the...

Title: Azure Store available to direct EA customers and channel partners
Summary: Azure Store is available to customers and channel partners subscribed to Azure via a direct Enterprise Agreement (EA). If you're an Azure EA customer in North America or Europe, you can purchase a range of application and data services from 3 rd party providers and your subscriptions will be automatically billed against your EA. Pricing for services in Azure Store is set by 3 rd party sellers. Store purchases are not eligible for Microsoft’s volume licensing discounts, and Azure monetary commitm...

Title: Scheduler GA pricing update
Summary: We announced General Availability for Scheduler at //Build 2014 last month. Today, the Scheduler GA pricing is officially in effect. Please see the pricing details page for more information.

Title: Traffic Manager support for external endpoints
Summary: Traffic Manager supports Azure endpoints and external endpoints, so you can control the distribution of user traffic to the endpoints you choose. Build highly available applications across Azure and on-premises, and apply intelligent traffic management policies across endpoints that live outside of Azure. For more information, visit the Traffic Manager page. To get a comprehensive look at pricing, visit the Traffic Manager Pricing Details page.

Title: Preview: Internal load balancing for virtual machines
Summary: Load balance your Azure virtual machines with private IP addresses. If your VM is in a virtual network, the internally load-balanced endpoint is accessible there. If it isn't, you can access it using a cloud service. Internal load balancing is useful when you’re creating multi-tier applications, and you want to load balance application tiers that aren't public facing. It's available in the VM standard tier at no additional cost. For more information, visit the Internal Load Balancing page.

Title: General Availability: Multiple site-to-site connections
Summary: Virtual Network supports more than one site-to-site connection, so you can securely connect multiple on-premises locations with a virtual network (VNet) in Azure. Using more than one connection doesn't cost extra - you only pay for the VNet gateway uptime. For more information, visit the Virtual Network website. To get a comprehensive look at pricing, visit the Virtual Network Pricing Details website.

Title: Preview: Azure RemoteApp
Summary: Azure RemoteApp delivers Windows Server session-based applications from Azure and helps IT to bring scale, agility and global access to their business applications. Users can access their applications remotely from anywhere and on a variety of devices. While appearing to run on the users' local device, the applications are centralized on Azure’s protected, reliable platform. With Azure RemoteApp, IT can enable users to access their corporate applications and stay productive on the go, scale up o...

Title: Preview: Azure Files
Summary: Use Azure Files with virtual machines to mount a shared file system using the SMB protocol. Your VMs can access the file system using standard Windows file APIs (CreateFile, ReadFile, WriteFile, etc.). VMs (or platform-as-a-service roles) can attach to these file systems concurrently, so you can share persistent data easily between various roles and instances. In addition to accessing your files through the Windows file APIs, you can access your data using the REST API (similar to the familiar B...

Title: Preview: API Management
Summary: Use Azure API Management to publish APIs reliably, securely, and at scale. Engage with and drive API consumption among developers, partners, and even internal teams while benefiting from the business and operational insights available in the portal. This service provides the tools that your organization needs to manage APIs - from provisioning user roles to creating usage plans and quotas, applying policies for transforming payloads, throttling, conducting analytics, monitoring, and configuring...

Title: General Availability: Compute-intensive A8 and A9 instances for virtual machines
Summary: New compute-intensive A8 and A9 instances for virtual machines provide faster processors, faster interconnectivity, more virtual cores for higher computing power, and larger amounts of memory. A8 instances (which have 8 virtual cores and 56 GB of RAM) and A9 instances (which have 16 virtual cores and 112 GB of RAM) also include a 40-Gbit/s InfiniBand network with remote direct memory access (RDMA) technology designed for parallel Message Passing Interface (MPI) applications. For more information...

Title: General Availability: ExpressRoute
Summary: Create private, high-throughput connections between Azure datacenters and your existing on-premises or hybrid infrastructure. ExpressRoute connections don’t use the public Internet, so they offer more reliability, faster speeds, lower latencies, and higher security than regular connections. We have a 99.9% SLA in place for connection uptime, and two new bandwidth tiers for Exchange Providers: 200 Mbps and 500 Mbps in addition to 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps tiers. ExpressRoute service will be available in...

Title: Preview: Redis Cache Service
Summary: Build highly scalable and responsive applications with Azure Redis Cache, a distributed, in-memory, managed cache based on the popular open-source Redis Cache . It gives you super-fast access to your data, is highly secured, managed by Microsoft, and is accessible from any application in Azure. Azure Redis Cache is available in the Azure Preview portal during public preview.

Title: April 2014 Cloud Services Guest OS Release completed
Summary: The April 2014 Guest OS release (versions 4.7, 3.14, 2.26, and 1.34), which incorporates all the latest MSRC updates, started release on May 2 and completed today (May 6). More information is available on the Guest OS Matrix page . Cloud service roles on automatic update will reboot once each to upgrade to the latest Guest OS. Guest OS updates only apply to Cloud Services. They do not apply to IaaS Virtual Machines.

Title: Azure SQL Database introduces new Basic, Standard, and Premium previews
Summary: Azure SQL Database introduces two new service tiers, Basic and Standard, to join Premium, which is already in preview. The Web and Business service editions will be retired in 12 months. The new tiers help deliver predictable performance across six performance levels for lightweight to heavyweight transactional application demands. Additionally, the new tiers offer a spectrum of business continuity features, a stronger uptime service-level agreement (SLA), larger database sizes for less money, a...

Title: Memcached Cloud available in the Azure Store
Summary: Redis Labs is now offering Memcached Cloud in the Azure Store. Memcached Cloud is a fully-managed service for running Memcached in a reliable and fail-safe manner. Your dataset is constantly replicated, so if a node fails, an auto-switchover mechanism guarantees data is served without interruption. Memcached Cloud provides various data persistence options as well as remote backups for disaster recovery purposes. After selecting Memcached Cloud in the Azure Store, it takes seconds to create your...

Title: Azure Brazil South region now in public preview
Summary: The Azure Brazil South region, located in Sao Paulo state, is broadly available for public preview (the final step before general availability). The new region means better performance and reduced latency for local customers, who can now keep their data in country if they opt for Locally Redundant Storage . While the region is in public preview, standard supplemental terms of use for Azure previews apply, meaning the Brazil South region (and all services hosted there) are excluded from service l...

Title: New Azure Web Sites region – Southeast Asia
Summary: Azure Web Sites recently expanded to Japan, and now we're adding Southeast Asia to our list of supported regions. Starting today, all customers will have the options to create their websites in the new region, with all Azure Web Sites’ great features available from day one. With the addition of this region, Azure Websites is now available in 4 different Asia regions: East Asia, Japan West, Japan East and Southeast Asia.

Title: Redis support on Azure available in the Azure Store
Summary: Redis Labs is now offering Redis Cloud in the Azure Store . Redis Cloud is a fully-managed cloud service for hosting and running your Redis dataset in a highly-available and scalable manner, with predictable and stable top performance. Redis Cloud offers true high-availability with its in-memory dataset replication and instant auto-failover mechanism, combined with its fast storage engine. Import an existing dataset to any of your Redis Cloud databases, from Azure blobs storage, FTP/HTTP server,...

Title: Cluster Operating System Update for HDInsight Clusters
Summary: HDInsight clusters created after April 3, 2014, have the following changes: Windows Server 2012 R2 (Azure OS Family 4) as the default OS on the cluster .NET 4.5 Updates to internal firewall rules Windows Server 2012 R2 This update moves HDInsight clusters to the most recent version of the OS. This enables greater performance and reliability, as well as the ability to integrate with OS features specific to OS Family 4 . .NET 4.5 As part of Windows Server 2012 R2, clusters now have .NET 4.5 availa...

Title: General Availability: Autoscale
Summary: Autoscale is now generally available. We've added new features since we first released it as a preview version: support for both performance- and schedule-based autoscaling, along with an API and .NET SDK so you can scale by any performance counters that you define. Autoscale supports all four Azure compute services: Cloud Services, Virtual Machines, Mobile Services and Web Sites. For Virtual Machines and Web Sites, Autoscale is included as a feature in the Standard mode, and for Mobile Services...

Title: General Availability: Azure Read-Access Geo Redundant Storage (RA-GRS)
Summary: Geo Redundant Storage accounts store data in two separate regions: The primary region (the default location where all updates and deletes are kept), and a secondary region (where copies of your data are stored). When you enable Azure Read-Access Geo Redundant Storage (RA-GRS), your application has Read-only access to the secondary region’s copy of the data in case your primary storage location fails.

Title: Azure Management Library 2.0.0-Preview for .NET and Node.js
Summary: In this preview release of Azure Management Library for .NET and Node.js, we're adding support for Azure Resource Manager. Create, manage, and deploy resource groups using local or gallery templates, search for and download gallery templates, and create and manage individual resources.

Title: General Availability: Scheduler
Summary: Azure Scheduler is live, available in all Azure regions, backed by an enterprise SLA, and ready to use for production scenarios. The release also includes new Azure Scheduler PowerShell cmdlets, and the Scheduler .NET API (included in WAML 1.0 ). Our customers used Scheduler (Preview) to invoke Hadoop workloads, trigger diagnostic cleanups, and periodically check that partners have submitted content on time. ISVs used it to add scheduling capabilities, like report generation and send reminders....

Title: Azure Cross Platform Command-Line Interface 0.8.0
Summary: In this release of Azure Cross Platform Command-Line Interface, we're adding support for Azure Resource Manager and Azure Active Directory authentication. Azure Resource Management support includes creating, managing, and deploying resource groups using local or gallery templates, search and download functionality for gallery templates, and creating and managing individual resources. Azure Active Directory authentication updates let you log in with a username and password from the console for an...

Title: New in Azure Web Sites: Web Hosting Plans
Summary: You can now create web hosting plans that let you share features like auto-scale, web tests, backup, and computing capacity across your web sites. Web hosting plans support a few pricing tiers (Free, Shared, Basic, and Standard) where each tier has its own capabilities. Sites in the same subscription and geographic location can share a web hosting plan. You can choose to have sites share a web hosting plan, or you can dedicate a web hosting plan to an individual site if that site requires dedica...

Title: New Basic SKU for Azure Web Sites
Summary: We've added a new Basic SKU tier (in addition to our current Free, Standard and Shared tiers) for customers who need more than the Shared tier offers. It includes scaling up to 3 dedicated instances, staging slots, and support for SSL. Plus, you'll run on a dedicated VM, but at a lower price than the Standard tier. If you need support for more instances (10), more shared storage (50 GB), site slots, or backup and restore, upgrade to the Standard tier.

Title: Resource groups in Azure Preview portal
Summary: Resource groups are a new concept in the Azure Preview portal. We think of them as "lifecycle boundaries," because when resources share a resource group, their lifecycles (from create, to update, to delete) are managed in an integrated way. Use resource groups to collect and manage all your application resources. Link resources across resource groups, share resources across lifecycle boundaries, and manage costs. View, monitor, and track your usage and billing for all the resources your applicat...

Title: New monitoring and operations features in Azure Web Sites
Summary: The Azure Portal preview adds new monitoring features for Azure Web Sites, including: View your site's streaming logs, and open a console to run commands against your site. Learn more . Create autoscale rules that use different metrics, and set up multiple scale-up or -down rules for the same metric. Learn more . Monitor memory working set (in bytes, per website), CPU percentage, memory percentage, HTTP queue length, and disk queue length to solve performance problems. Customize the charts in th...

Title: Puppet Extension is now available for Azure
Summary: Puppet Enterprise is IT automation software that gives system administrators the power to easily automate repetitive tasks, quickly deploy critical applications, and proactively manage infrastructure. The Puppet Agent installed with this Azure extension fetches configurations from a Puppet Master server, and reports events to the Puppet Enterprise Console, a graphical interface that visualizes infrastructure changes across the organization. This extension is published by Puppet Labs .

Title: New Azure billing features
Summary: Billing is now part of every service blade in the Preview portal. We’ve created Billing journeys that help you slice and dice your billing info and turn it into charts and visualizations that give you at-a-glance insights into each of your subscriptions. When you open your Start board, you’ll see a high-level summary of your subscriptions. Dive into the Billing summary to see overall subscription status, the current charges over time, and the next due date for running charges. Individual subscri...

Title: Visual Studio Online is now integrated with the Azure portal
Summary: Manage your development lifecycle with Visual Studio Online in the Azure portal. Create a Team Project to collaborate with others, host your source code, track work items, monitor builds, and continuously deploy to Azure Websites. Start your next development project in the cloud – 5 users are free! Learn more

Title: First-of-its-kind Microsoft Azure Preview portal
Summary: The Azure Preview portal's all-in-one, work-anywhere experience combines developer and infrastructure services to radically simplify DevOps, whether you write code, operate infrastructure, or manage finances. To learn more about the Preview portal, check out this 3 minute video .

Title: Azure Active Directory App Gallery
Summary: Add and manage over 1000 apps using Azure Active Directory. Check out the list of apps , or add an app using the Azure Management portal to see it in the app gallery.

Title: New service: Automation (Preview)
Summary: Use Azure Automation (now in public preview) to create, monitor, deploy, and maintain resources in your Azure environment. It automates time-consuming, error-prone, and frequently repeated cloud operations tasks (for both Azure and third party systems). Visit Scott Guthrie’s blog and the Automation page to learn more about Automation and how to get started.

Title: Standard tier pricing changes for Azure Web Sites
Summary: Now that we've introduced the Basic pricing tier, we're making some improvements to the Standard tier. We're increasing the storage quota from 10 GB to 50 GB, adding 5 free SNI SSL and dedicated IP to each subscription, and removing the Web Socket 350 connection limit. Changes take effect in April 2014.

Title: Java support on Microsoft Azure Web Sites
Summary: Beginning in April, Azure Web Sites supports hosting Java web applications. You won't have to make a ton of configuration changes - when you're done, you can send all incoming site HTTP traffic to the Java HTTP listen port. Use the Azure Portal to create Java 7 websites with Apache Tomcat 7.0.50 or Jetty 9.1.0 and upload a .WAR file. Get more advanced with complete installs of Apache Tomcat or Jetty (available in the application gallery), and create a web container you can configure for your web...

Title: Wildcard domains in Azure Web Sites
Summary: Combine wildcard domains with SNI SSL to secure all your subdomains, without creating individual bindings. To add a wildcard hostname, point a wildcard CNAME record to your site just like you would for a regular hostname (e.g., "*.contoso.com"). Then use Azure's domain configuration to add that domain to your site.

Title: Irregular sign-in notifications added to Azure Active Directory Premium
Summary: Azure Active Directory identifies your normal user sign-in patterns. When a sign-in falls outside the norm, it's included in a report and your administrators are notified. Learn more about these notifications (and other reporting and analytics tools in Azure Active Directory and Azure Active Directory Premium) in the Active Directory team blog .

Title: Azure PowerShell 0.8.0
Summary: In this release of Azure PowerShell, we're adding support for Azure Resource Manager, Scheduler and a bunch of infrastructure cmdlet improvements. Azure Resource Management support includes creating and managing resource groups and resource group deployments using local or gallery templates, search and download functionality for gallery templates, and creating and managing individual resources. Azure Scheduler support includes creating and managing job collections and HTTP and storage queue jobs...

Title: VM Images replace OS Images
Summary: VM Image is the new and improved image entity and replaces OS Images. It includes the OS disk, and adds data disks. Capture a VM (running or shut down) to create a VM Image. The underlying operating system may be generalized (for example, sys prep has been run for Windows or `waagent –deprovision’ executed for Linux - like an OS Image today), or specialized (where the provisioning information remains intact). Once captured, use a VM Image to deploy new VMs. Think of the generalized VM Image as a...

Title: Azure Active Directory Premium
Summary: You can subscribe to Azure Active Directory Premium starting today. Azure Active Directory Premium subscribers can leverage: Self-service password reset Self-service group management Group-based application access management Multi-factor authentication Customized branding Reporting, alerting and analytics Learn more about Azure Active Direct Premium (including how to subscribe) on the Active Directory team blog .

Title: Management Libraries for .NET
Summary: The Management Libraries for .NET include managed wrappers around the Microsoft Azure Service Management REST APIs . These libraries give .NET developers a client-side SDK written as Portable Class Libraries (PCL), so if you're writing applications for desktop applications in .NET, Windows 8.1 Store applications, or Windows Phone 8 applications, you can automate the provisioning or management of Microsoft Azure assets. Use the Management Libraries for .NET to write integration tests that provisi...

Title: Azure Active Directory Premium: Self-service group management
Summary: Self-service group management is now available to Azure Active Directory Premium subscribers. Your employees can add and manage cloud based security groups, and these groups can be used to assign access to applications. Learn more on the Active Directory team blog .

Title: General Availability: Azure in China
Summary: We've partnered with 21Vianet - one of the largest Internet service providers in China - to bring Azure's public cloud services to Chinese customers. Visit the Official Microsoft Blog for more information on today’s announcement.

Title: General Availability: Hadoop 2 in Azure HDInsight
Summary: Hadoop 2.2 in Azure HDInsight is now generally available. Easily deploy the latest version of key Hadoop components (including YARN, Hive, Pig, Oozie and others) to Azure and bring big data processing to all of the data in Azure Blob Storage. This release includes improved performance and scalability of the core Map/Reduce implementation, the ability to use YARN to bring different distributed apps to the cluster, and substantial performance improvements in Hive via the second phase of the Stinge...

Title: Reduced Pricing on Storage
Summary: We're reducing prices by up to 20% for Block Blobs Storage and Disks/Page Blobs Storage, up to 28% for Locally Redundant Disks/Page Blobs Storage, and reducing the price of Azure Storage transactions by 50%. These pricing reductions are in effect for all regions worldwide. Learn more on the Azure Storage pricing page .

Title: General Availability: Oracle software on Azure
Summary: Oracle Database, Oracle WebLogic Server, and Java are now generally available with license-included virtual machine images, and you can find them in the Azure Virtual Machines image gallery. Whether you’re an Oracle administrator or a Java developer, you have full Oracle support. Learn more at Azure.com .

Title: Azure Traffic Manager now supports Azure Web Sites
Summary: Azure Traffic Manager is extending support to manage and load balance Azure Web sites. This feature is available for all web sites in the Standard tier. This integration brings the benefits of Traffic Manager, previously available only for Cloud Services, to Azure Web sites-based deployments. Key Traffic Manager scenarios now enabled for Azure Web sites include: High availability : Use multiple deployments in separate data centers, with built-in health monitoring and automatic failover Improved...

Title: New Azure datacenters available in Japan
Summary: We've opened two new Azure datacenters in Japan: Japan East (in Saitama Prefecture) and Japan West (in Osaka Prefecture). Both officially launched in February and were built to help customers meet data residency goals, improve data durability, and address disaster recovery scenarios via geo-replication between the two regions. Visit the Microsoft Azure website for details on service availability and pricing . Read the Official Microsoft Blog for more background info on the launch.

Title: Azure Web Sites now supports WebJobs
Summary: Run custom jobs (using executables or scripts) on your web site. WebJobs supports running jobs on demand, continuously, or on a schedule, and automates administrative or recurring tasks. See How to Use the WebJobs feature in Azure Web Sites to learn more.

Title: Service Health Notifications added to the Management Portal
Summary: Azure Incident Notifications now displayed within the Azure Management Portal. Customers will see a toast in the Portal for the following major types of ongoing (i.e. “Active”) incidents, with the option to open a pop-up with more information about the incident. Partial Performance Degradation Partial Service Interruption Full Performance Degradation Full Service Interruption Advisory Learn more about Azure Service Notifications .

Title: Remove standard server headers in Azure Web Sites
Summary: HTTP headers are part of the communication process between web servers and browsers, and are included in the request and response. One example is the server header, which lists the product name and version of the web server (e.g., Microsoft-IIS/8.0 ). All web servers generate these headers, but now you can disable them on Azure Web Sites. You need to update your site’s web.config file to remove headers. Learn how on the Azure team blog .

Title: Backup and restore for Azure Web Sites
Summary: Save a snapshot version of your web app (along with any SQL or MySQL databases it uses) and start your site backup. You decide when a backup starts - manually, or automatically on a schedule you choose (for example, once a day at midnight). Later, restore a website to a previous version, or create a new website based on one of your original site's backups. Backup and Restore is available at no additional cost to all Web Site customers using our Standard Tier.

Title: New extension shows virtual machine info
Summary: The recent VM Agent release includes an extension that displays Windows virtual machine info on the desktop of the VM instance (when you RDP into it). It's a quick way to see VM configuration settings (internal and public IP, disk space, memory, deployment ID, etc).

Title: New service: ExpressRoute (Preview)
Summary: ExpressRoute (now in public preview) is a dedicated, private, high-throughput network connection between Azure datacenters and on-premises IT environments. Connect your existing datacenters to Azure without flowing any traffic over the public Internet. Network quality-of-service is guaranteed. Use Azure as a natural extension of an existing private network or datacenter. Start today with dedicated connections though Equinix datacenters, add Azure services to MPLS VPN provided by AT&T, or (throug...

Title: Virtual Machines support VM Agents for Windows and Linux
Summary: VM Agent support for IaaS Virtual Machines helps you manage your Windows and Linux VMs. It's a lightweight process that runs inside your virtual machines - use it to install and manage your extensions (software that extends the functionality of a VM and helps you work through common management tasks).

Title: Co-admin limit increased
Summary: In February, we increased the co-administrators limit for each Azure subscription to 200 (up from 10). This will make it easier for large teams to share a single Azure subscription, and will simplify subscription management.

Title: Mobile Services integrated with Notification Hubs
Summary: Mobile Services integration with Notification Hubs adds tags and tag expressions for advanced targeting, includes broadcast push support at high scale, and adds template support for personalization and localization. Learn more on Scott Guthrie's blog , or get started with our Push tutorial .

Title: Mobile Services support for .NET backend
Summary: Write backend Mobile Service logic by using .NET and the ASP.NET Web API framework. Use the ASP.NET Web API, Visual Studio, and Mobile Services to build great mobile apps, and integrate features such as mobile authentication and push notifications. Use Web API features such as the OData controller and third-party Web API-based frameworks such as Breeze, and debug your Mobile Services .NET backend by using Visual Studio (running locally on your computer or remotely in Azure). Mobile Services runs...

Title: PhoneGap support for Azure Mobile services
Summary: A new integrated PhoneGap Quick Start in the Azure management portal makes developing cross-platform mobile apps with PhoneGap and Azure Mobile Services easier. Check out the Getting Started with Mobile Services for PhoneGap tutorial to learn more.

Title: AutoHeal for Azure Web Sites
Summary: AutoHeal recycles the worker process for your site based on settings you choose (like configuration changes, requests, memory-based limits, or the time needed to execute a request).

Title: WordPress in the Azure Web Sites App Gallery updated to version 3.8
Summary: WordPress 3.8, code named "Parker" (in honor of bebop innovator Charlie Parker) is now available in the Azure Web Sites App Gallery. WordPress 3.8 is a major facelift compared to previous versions, with a modern, flat, and uncluttered design, clean typography using Open Sans typeface, and a colorful Admin Dashboard. With Parker, WordPress also adapts better to different platforms, and displays better with faster rendering thanks to vector-based icons. In addition, WordPress 3.8’s theme managemen...

Title: General Availability: A8 and A9 compute-intensive instances for Azure Cloud Services
Summary: Two new Cloud Services instances are now available: A8 includes 8 virtual cores with 56 gigabytes (GB) of memory, and A9 features 16 virtual cores with 112 GB. A8 and A9 are "compute-intensive instances," with faster processors and more virtual cores for higher compute power and larger amounts of memory. Plus, they feature a 40 GB/S InfiniBand network with remote direct memory access (RDMA) designed for parallel Message Passing Interface (MPI) applications. Compute-intensive instances are ideal...

Title: Mobile Services Integration with Sencha Touch
Summary: We've partnered with Sencha to add support for SenchaTouch to Mobile Services. SenchaTouch is an HTML/JavaScript-based development framework for building cross-platform mobile apps and websites. With today’s addition, you can add Mobile Services to your SenchaTouch app. Get started , or learn more on the Sencha extension resources page .

Title: ISO Certification expanded to include more Azure services
Summary: Azure has successfully completed its annual ISO audit. In addition to Cloud Services, Storage, Virtual Machines and Virtual Networks, the scope of the audit increased to include SQL Database, Active Directory, Traffic Manager, Web Sites, BizTalk Services, Media Services, Mobile Services, Service Bus, Multi-Factor Authentication, and HDInsight. Visit the Trust Center for a full list.

Title: More services add alerts
Summary: Alerts are now available for Web Sites and SQL Databases, in addition to Cloud Services, Virtual Machines, Mobile Services, and Storage. Create alerts for Web Sites based on any metric in the portal, including errors, CPU time and total requests. Create storage alerts for Web and Business tier SQL Databases, and CPU Cores and IOPS alerts for SQL Database Premium (Preview). To get started with Alerting, click on the Management Services extension on the left navigation tab of the Windows Azure Man...

Title: Staged deployments on Azure Web Sites
Summary: Set up staged publishing by creating multiple site slots for Standard mode websites. A staging site slot is created for each default production site, and you can swap slots with no downtime. See Staged Publishing on Azure Web Sites to learn more.

Title: Minute-by-minute site metrics for Azure Web Sites
Summary: View changes in your site metrics at the minute level, so you can debug issues as they happen (instead of seeing changes aggregated over hours or days). Learn how on the Azure team blog .

Title: Azure Web Sites adds Always On
Summary: Websites unload if they sit idle for too long, which helps the system conserve resources. The new Always On setting (available for Standard tier websites) keeps your site up and running, which translates to higher availability and faster response times across the board. Click the Configure tab to enable Always On.

Title: General Availability: Hyper-V Recovery Manager
Summary: Hyper-V Recovery Manager is generally available, includes full support and an SLA, and is ready for IT Admins to use in production. Protect important services by replicating and recovering System Center 2012 private clouds at a secondary location. We released updates in January 2014 that include support for: Improved Failback : Failback support is improved when the primary host cluster is rebuilt after an outage. Kerberos based Authentication : Cloud configuration supports Kerberos-based authent...

Title: General Availability: Traffic Manager
Summary: Leverage the load balancing capabilities of Azure Traffic Manager to create highly responsive and highly available production grade applications. Traffic Manager carries a service level agreement of 99.99%, and is supported through your existing Windows Azure support plan. We are also announcing new pricing for Traffic Manager. Free promotional pricing will remain in effect until December 31, 2013. To learn more, check out Scott Guthrie's blog and the Traffic Manager page.
